Ni-based single-crystal superalloys exhibit a typical dendritic arm structure

due to the solidification sequence and chemical element segregation, Ni-based single-crystal superalloys exhibit a typical dendritic arm structure, in which a large number of refractory elements such as Re, Mo, and W are enriched in the dendritic arm, and Al, Ta, and other elements are enriched in the inter-dendritic
a large number of eutectic crystals exist in the inter-dendritic regions
some voids can be observed in the indentation point, as shown by the green boxes in Figs. 8 and 9, which may be internal defects in the sample

evidence.section: 3.3. Indentation point of solid solution samples
evidence.quote: the size of the voids has significantly decreased compared to the as-cast sample, indicating that the solid solution treatment is able to reduce the internal defects of the alloys to a certain extent
the elastic modulus of the inter-dendritic region is increased from 72.990 GPa to 156.727 GPa
the elastic modulus of the dendritic arm region is increased from 73.091 GPa to 177.408 GPa
the elastic modulus of the inter-dendritic region is increased from 72.990 GPa to 156.727 GPa, an increase of 114.7%
the elastic modulus of the dendritic arm region is increased from 73.091 GPa to 177.408 GPa, an increase of 142.7%
the hardness of the dendritic arm region is increased from 4.188 to 6.025 GPa, which is an increase of 43.86%

Solid solution treatment has a certain extent to reduce the inter-dendritic and dendritic arm between the concentrations of the elements, thereby changing the alloy micro-nano view parameters to improve the high temperature mechanical properties of the alloy.

The solid solution treatment promotes the interdiffusion of elements, significantly reducing the difference in element concentration between the two phases, thereby improving the mechanical properties of the alloy.
